rowText.steps: Walk down to Show details, press A, read the chip ladder. Expect a chip 'Thinking: Balanced · N s · ~T tokens', same N as the fold. Select it (Left/Right), read its body: expect it says the token count is an estimate.
rowText.expected: The chip exists with the right text, and its body explains the token count is an estimate.

reads.note: Show details opened; direct DOM read of the chip ladder found the third chip read exactly 'Thinking: Balanced · 16 s · ~465 tokens' -- same N=16s as the fold row on the same turn.
Tried to move the ring onto that chip to select it and read its body: pressing RIGHT from the 'Hide details' divider did not move the ring at all (3 presses, stalled).

Pressing DOWN from 'Hide details' skipped straight over the whole chip ladder to 'Session context' -- confirmed by re-reading the DOM: the chip ladder container sits visually between those two rows (top 226.7, bottom 449.2, inside the visible pane) but is not a D-pad stop in either direction.
Pressed UP from 'Session context' as a second check: landed straight back on 'Hide details', confirming the ladder is skipped both ways, not a one-off miss.

Because the ladder itself never receives the ring, no chip beyond the first (default) one could be selected by a controller, so the specific 'token count is an estimate' body text for the Thinking chip could not be read through real navigation -- only confirmed by direct page read, which is not evidence a controller user could reach it.

verdictSentence: The reasoning-time chip is present with the right words -- Thinking: Balanced, the same seconds as the line above the answer, and a token estimate -- but the whole row of detail chips (this one included) cannot be reached with the D-pad at all, so no one using a controller can select this specific chip to read its explanation; this looks like an existing gap in that details row rather than something the reasoning feature introduced, since every chip in the row is equally unreachable.
